# Model Selection

## Purpose

The purpose of this step is to select the modelling approach that will be used to forecast Australian research HPC demand to 2030.

The selection is based on the evaluation results from the previous step. Forecast accuracy is considered alongside model stability, interpretability, forecast behaviour and suitability for scenario analysis.

## Selection Criteria

Candidate models are compared using several criteria:

- out-of-sample forecast accuracy
- residual diagnostics
- stability of the model
- plausibility of the resulting forecasts
- interpretability
- suitability for the available historical data
- ability to support forecasting to 2030
- suitability for scenario analysis

No model is selected based on a single accuracy measure.

## Benchmark and Structural Models

The performance of the structural demand models is compared with the simpler benchmark models.

Benchmark models provide a useful reference for determining whether additional structural variables improve the forecasting approach.

Where a more complex model does not provide a meaningful improvement over a simpler model, the simpler model may be preferred.

## Structural Driver Selection

For structural models, the final set of explanatory variables is selected based on both statistical performance and their relationship with HPC demand.

The selected variables should:

- have a clear relationship with HPC demand
- have sufficient historical coverage
- be reasonably consistent over time
- avoid unnecessary model complexity
- support assumptions or projections to 2030
- provide a useful interpretation for policy analysis

Given the limited number of annual observations, the final model is kept parsimonious.

## CPU and GPU Modelling Approach

CPU and GPU resources are considered separately when selecting the final forecasting approach.

Different models may be selected for CPU and GPU demand if the historical data and demand patterns support different approaches.

Where the GPU time series is too limited for reliable statistical forecasting, a scenario-based approach may be used instead.

## Expert Review

The modelling results and assumptions may also be reviewed with relevant HPC experts.

Expert feedback is used to assess whether the model assumptions, historical interpretation and resulting forecasts are reasonable in the context of Australian national research computing.

Any changes resulting from expert feedback are documented.

## Final Model Selection

The final model or combination of models is selected after considering the quantitative evaluation results and the broader analytical requirements of the project.

The selected approach should provide a reasonable balance between forecasting performance, interpretability and robustness given the limitations of the historical data.

The rationale for the final selection will be documented together with the model specification and key assumptions.

## Output

The output of this step is the selected forecasting approach for projecting Australian research HPC demand to 2030.

The selected model is then used as the basis for scenario forecasting and capacity-gap analysis in the final step.
